items.transcript: A lot of other cleaners will disagree with this. I love the chaotic clients. I love the people who call frantically that need a clean today because their cleaner didn't show up on them. I love the move-out cleans where I get a call from the property manager and they're like, we went with somebody else. However, they didn't do a good job, but the new tenants are moving in tomorrow. Can you fit it in today? I'm like, yes, we can. We can just come swoop in like a nine shining armor and literally solve all of their problems. And they're going to walk into that unit or they're going to walk into their house and they're going to be like, it's like going to be like the angel gates are opening. They're like, oh my God. And they like cry and they call us and they thank us. And I love being that person. Anyway, the way that we're able to do that without getting lots and lots of complaints, because that I think is usually the thing that drives cleaners away from the last minute like chaos. It tends to be the kind of people who complain. I actually think that that's usually a sales motion because the day of you're trying to book that client, everything gets like fast tracked. So you skip your cleaning agreement, you skip the walkthrough, you skip your normal sales pitch. You kind of do things to make the process go faster. But I have a very simple, easy way to go through the exact same process that we go through with everybody else. That way we can fit in the last minute chaotic clients, increase our revenue, keep those clients on for recurring because we were just their nine shining armor. And yeah, everybody's happy. And I'm able to do that through Jobber. It's super duper simple. So essentially all we do is the same sales motion. So we take them through a walkthrough. I'm able to get all the specifications from the client to know what exactly needs done. That is then going to be translated over into their Jobber profile. Their Jobber profile is going to have two sections to it. Actually three. The first two sections are going to be the notes within the profile. We're going to have two separate notes, one cleaner specific note and one admin only note. The cleaner specific note will be what the cleaners actually see on site. You can see everything listed here with just important notes that they'll definitely need to be able to complete the clean. Then down here, you're going to see the internal admin notes. These are potentially notes that we just don't need or want the cleaning team to see. There is also a special checklist that gets put into their Jobber profile. That checklist is going to be specifically built for that home. I would highly recommend Jobber. It is what I use in my cleaning company for what, five years. And I always recommend when I see somebody using a different software to switch over because this literally is so simple and has everything that you need. If you want to try Jobber for free, make sure to click the link in my bio.

items.transcript: Let's see what cleaning products we can get at Lowe's that are actually cruelty-free. Okay, so the first one that I'm coming across is Zep. So I'm actually seeing here that Zep is cruelty-free according to the brand. However, it is not certified leaping bunny. There's no certification basically verifying that they are actually cruelty-free, which is really important. Fabuloso. I wouldn't recommend using Fabuloso. However, I know a lot of people do, so let's see if they are cruelty-free. Oh, interesting. So Fabuloso is actually a UK-based brand, not a US-based brand. So I didn't know that. I will look into it and I'll put on the screen if they're technically certified cruelty-free in the US as well. Bona. This is a popular brand that I used to use when I owned my cleaning company. Let's see if they are cruelty-free. Okay, looks like Bona does state that they are cruelty-free so they don't test on animals. However, they're not certified by Leaping Bunny. So again, that's another situation where it's not actually verified by a third party. Ooh, Sprayway Glass Cleaner. This one, oh my gosh, me and my mom used that literally when we started the cleaning company like years, years and years ago. And I know a lot of cleaners who still use this product. It's super popular. So let's see if it's cruelty-free. So I am seeing just like straight away that they are not certified cruelty-free and they don't claim to be. It actually shows that their aerosols are tested on rats and rabbits. Ooh, Windex. Okay, that is going like throwing it back. I have not used Windex in forever, but I know it's still like a pretty popular brand, of course. So let's look it up, see if it's cruelty-free. So it is not cruelty-free. Unfortunately, it is owned by a parent company that animal tests, a pretty popular one, which you'll see on the Walmart shelves, SC Johnson. So I would definitely avoid SC Johnson. Pledge. So we didn't actually use any like dusting product. We would usually just use like warm water to dust. But Pledge is, I know, a really popular one. It is unfortunately not cruelty-free because it is also owned by SC Johnson. So definitely would not use that product if you want to go cruelty-free. Ooh, okay, last but not least is Pine Sol. So it is not cruelty-free, unfortunately. It is owned by Clorox, which is a brand that definitely animal tests. All right, that wraps us up for Lowe's.
